summary.headline: Manaksia Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 86% QoQ to INR29.08 crore (11.06% margin), with record EBITDA/ton of INR10,400 on Alu-Zinc ramp-up.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR263 crore, up 15% QoQ and about 3.6% YoY, with realisation up nearly 12% QoQ to INR88,597/ton on mix and new-order pricing. PAT rose 163% QoQ to INR14.10 crore (5.36% margin). Management said all new Q1 orders are priced to cover current raw material and freight costs plus a margin buffer. Volumes were slightly down YoY (about 27,900 t vs about 29,000 t), which management attributed to Alu-Zinc ramp-up teething issues rather than demand. The second colour coating line and 7 MW solar plant are targeted for Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR79,180/ton in Q4 FY26, nearly +12%

segments.name: Pre-Painted Steel
segments.commentary: Production 20,510 t at 95.4% utilisation on the existing line; 74% of Q1 sales volume. Pre-painted exports grew 25% YoY.

segments.name: Alu-Zinc
segments.commentary: Production 27,941 t, up 8% QoQ, on the new line running at 62% utilisation; 26% of Q1 sales. Galvanised steel sales were nil in Q1 as the shift to Alu-Zinc was completed in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 65% of total volume, 18,221 t. Export revenue grew 20% YoY. Four new markets added in Q1: Latvia, Brazil, Jamaica and Somalia.

guidance_outlook: Second colour coating line (Pre-painted capacity 86,000 to 236,000 tpa, +174%) and 7 MW captive solar plant (offsets 50-55% of Kutch grid power) both targeted for Q2 FY27.
Alu-Zinc Phase 1 utilisation expected to reach 75-80% in about 3 more months; second colour coating line expected 50-60% utilisation in H2 FY27.
FY27 tonnage of about 150,000 t and revenue of INR1,300-1,350 crore assumed on new capacity at 50-60% utilisation.
FY28 tonnage of 180,000-200,000 t and revenue of INR1,700-1,750 crore targeted; a separate analyst question quoted 1.80-2.10 lakh t and INR1,700-1,800 crore.
Management guided to EBITDA margin of about 1-2% further growth on top of 11%, but said it is too early to say whether that is reached in FY27. Management does not expect a dip in EBITDA in Q2.
Phase 2 (cold rolling backward integration plus second Alu-Zinc line) estimated at INR350 crore; peak Alu-Zinc revenue after Phase 2 INR2,500-2,700 crore on about 3 lakh t.
capex_capacity: Capex already concluded of about INR140 crore (Alu-Zinc technology upgrade, second colour coating line, solar plant), mostly in CWIP and to be capitalised within Q2 FY27; only INR15-20 crore of debt remains to be deployed.
Current debt about INR115 crore, including term debt for these projects; peak debt estimated at INR125-130 crore given ongoing repayments.

Phase 2 capex INR350 crore, funded by internal accruals, debt and equity; additional debt estimated at about INR100 crore, not yet frozen. Management expects debt-equity not to exceed 1.25x (currently just above 1x).
Phase 2 cold rolling unit is in FY28 and is expected to cut working capital cycle from about 75 days to single-digit days by reducing SKU inventory.
Salesforce CRM implementation underway. Planned GSPC natural gas pipeline agreement in Gujarat to diversify away from LPG.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR450 crore (plus or minus INR20-25 crore), execution time 4.5-5 months; management guided a continuous 3-5 month book, around INR350-450 crore for the rest of FY27.
Order flow is largely repetitive quarterly orders from long-term export and domestic OEM customers, backed by annual offtake MoUs; Deepesh's note said about 80% of the order book is export.
Pricing is reset every quarter with export customers, passing through raw material, freight and energy changes. Management said most raw material is booked against orders in hand.
Q1 volume shortfall attributed to Alu-Zinc ramp-up pace, not demand. Pre-painted line ran at 95.4% utilisation.
Incremental EBITDA from galvanised to Alu-Zinc estimated at INR1,000-3,000/ton, from both lower cost and a price premium.
LPG/propane prices spiked from about INR60/kg to INR200/kg during the Iran war and Hormuz disruption, and have eased to about INR80/kg, roughly 25% above pre-war levels.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the record EBITDA/ton and how much can it rise after solar and CCL2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Alu-Zinc ramp-up, export tonnage and higher realisation drove INR10,400/ton. Further margin upside is possible if the capacity additions and solar plant execute well.

qa_highlights.question: How is the capex funded and how much is spent?
qa_highlights.answer: Total planned Phase 2 capex is INR350 crore, funded by a mix of internal accruals, debt and equity. Around INR140 crore is concluded, largely in CWIP; additional debt about INR100 crore is an estimate, and leverage is capped at 1.25x debt-equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volume fall YoY from about 29,000 t to about 27,900 t?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed 100% of the shortfall to Alu-Zinc ramp-up pace (teething issues for 3-4 months), not demand. It expects utilisation to reach 75-80% in about 3 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle and how will it change?
qa_highlights.answer: The cycle is about 75 days after creditors. The cold rolling unit (Phase 2, FY28) is expected to halve inventory and compress the cycle to single-digit days.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 revenue and tonnage targets?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27: about 150,000 t and INR1,300-1,350 crore on new capacity at 50-60% utilisation in H2. FY28: 180,000-200,000 t and INR1,700-1,750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a supply risk from the LPG/Hormuz disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Buffer stock kept the plant running nonstop. Supply was diversified to private as well as PSU suppliers at extra cost, and LPG prices have eased to about INR80/kg from INR200/kg peak.

risks_watch: Alu-Zinc Phase 1 ramp-up is still at 62% utilisation; delays would hold back volumes and the INR1,300-1,350 crore FY27 revenue plan.
Heavy working capital and receivables/inventory build-up, with cash flow directed to capex and working capital during scale-up.
Fuel (LPG/propane) price and supply volatility; the GSPC natural gas pipeline agreement is still being signed.
Commissioning of the second colour coating line and solar plant in Q2 FY27; ramp-up timing for CCL2 (50-60% in H2).
Phase 2 funding not frozen (INR350 crore, additional debt about INR100 crore); execution and leverage risk.
Management's guidance on FY27 EBITDA margin of about 12% was not firmly confirmed; it said it is hard to be precise.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margins, pricing discipline and capacity ramp-up, but cautious on specifics: management declined to give precise FY27 margin or Phase 2 timing and said several figures are estimates. Some Q&A answers were unclear, including the order-intake and EBITDA-peak questions.
key_quotes: This quarter, the plant ran without any disruption.
all the new orders in Q1 were priced to fully cover the current cost environment with the margin buffer on top.
And this is 100% attributable to the pace of ramp-up of the Alu-Zinc line.
So demand or ability to sell is not a concern for us at all.

growth.why: FY27 guided to about 150,000 t and INR1,300-1,350 crore revenue, backed by the Alu-Zinc ramp (62% utilised, targeted 75-80% in ~3 months), a second colour coating line (+174% pre-painted capacity) targeted for Q2 FY27, and an order book of about INR450 crore (3-5 months continuous).
